headline: Pretrained genomic and mRNA models adapted for regulatory and modification prediction
label: Pretrained Biological Sequence Models
summary: Sequence foundation models are now specialized for modifications, regulatory marks, and mRNA regions, making evaluation design decisive.
synthesis: These studies share a common move: pretrained sequence encoders are repurposed for specific downstream readouts rather than used as generic embeddings. RawMod applies a transformer to nanopore raw-signal pileups to detect DNA base modifications without a control sample, learning all modification types within one model. The apicomplexan GPN model, trained on 455 assemblies, improves epigenomic prediction in Plasmodium falciparum, especially when labeled data are scarce. ModBERT pretrains on a five-letter probabilistic genome encoding variants and CpG methylation from long-read data to predict regulatory activity. The mRNA study challenges global pooling itself, averaging embeddings separately over 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR and introducing a region-aware benchmark. The lightweight CNN separating coding from intergenomic sequence, at 91.87% validation accuracy, is the most conventional entry. What is new is the explicit encoding of modification and region structure into either the input representation or the readout.
